mcqs.learning_point: Understand the meaning of parallel lines
mcqs.question: Which of the following best describes parallel lines?

options.A: Lines that intersect at a point
options.B: Lines that are the same line
options.C: Lines that never meet, no matter how far extended
options.D: Lines that form a right angle

mcqs.answer: Lines that never meet, no matter how far extended
mcqs.explanation: Parallel lines are two distinct straight lines that are in the same plane and never intersect, no matter how far they are extended. Option C states this definition. Option A describes intersecting lines, B describes coincident lines, and D describes perpendicular lines.

mcqs.question: If two lines are drawn on a sheet of paper and they never meet, which term describes them?
mcqs.explanation: When two lines in the same plane never intersect, they are called parallel lines. Option C is correct. Intersecting lines meet at a point, perpendicular lines meet at a right angle, and skew lines are non‑coplanar, which is not considered at this grade level.

mcqs.question: In a diagram, line AB is drawn horizontally, line CD is also drawn horizontally, and line EF is drawn vertically. Which pair of lines are parallel?
mcqs.explanation: Lines AB and CD are both horizontal, so they have the same direction and will never meet; therefore they are parallel. The vertical line EF is not parallel to the horizontal lines. Options A and B pair a horizontal with a vertical line, which are perpendicular, not parallel. Option D repeats A.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise parallel lines in everyday surroundings
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an example of parallel lines that you can see in everyday life?

options.A: The edges of a closed book
options.B: The sides of a road lane
options.C: The hands of a clock at 3 o'clock

mcqs.answer: The sides of a road lane
mcqs.explanation: The two edges that bound a lane of a road run in the same direction and never meet, making them parallel. The edges of a closed book meet at the spine, the clock hands intersect at the centre, and the sides of a triangle meet at vertices, so they are not parallel.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand the meaning of parallel lines
mcqs.question: Railway tracks consist of two long metal rails. Which statement correctly explains why these rails are parallel?

options.A: They are drawn on the same line
options.B: They are always the same distance apart and never meet
options.C: They intersect at a point far away
options.D: They are perpendicular to each other

mcqs.answer: They are always the same distance apart and never meet
mcqs.explanation: Parallel lines keep a constant distance between them and never intersect, which is exactly how railway rails are designed. Option A describes a single line, C is false for parallel lines, and D describes perpendicular lines.

mcqs.question: A student wants to draw a second line that is parallel to a given line on graph paper. Which action will guarantee the new line is parallel?

options.A: Draw the second line with the same slope as the first line
options.B: Draw the second line intersecting the first line at a right angle
options.C: Draw the second line with a different slope
options.D: Draw the second line overlapping the first line

mcqs.answer: Draw the second line with the same slope as the first line
mcqs.explanation: In a coordinate plane, lines that have the same slope are parallel because they rise and run at the same rate and therefore never meet. Option B creates perpendicular lines, C gives intersecting lines, and D makes the same line, not a distinct parallel line.

mcqs.question: A student says, “If two lines are far apart, they must be parallel.” Which response correctly addresses this misconception?

options.A: True, distance alone makes lines parallel
options.B: False, lines must have the same direction and never meet
options.C: True, any two lines that do not touch are parallel
options.D: False, only lines that intersect are parallel

mcqs.answer: False, lines must have the same direction and never meet
mcqs.explanation: Parallelism depends on direction, not on how far apart the lines are. Two lines can be far apart and still intersect if extended. Therefore option B correctly refutes the misconception. Options A and C are incorrect statements, and D misdefines parallel lines.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise parallel lines in everyday surroundings
mcqs.question: You look at a rectangular garden whose opposite sides are straight. Which reasoning shows that the opposite sides are parallel?

options.B: They are opposite each other and never meet
options.C: They are both made of wood

mcqs.answer: They are opposite each other and never meet
mcqs.explanation: In a rectangle, each pair of opposite sides are parallel because they lie in the same plane, have the same direction, and never intersect, even if extended. Option B captures this geometric property. Option A may be true in a particular orientation but does not guarantee parallelism. Options C and D are irrelevant to parallelism.
